summary: Standby pool handoff strips tenant model pin and prevents canary cohort from receiving promoted variant
description:
Issue summary: BrightHealth reports that after a regional spillover event (us-west), their tenant-bound model pin to gptj-redwood-v2-16k is intermittently lost when traffic is routed to the regional standby pool. This results in the tenant receiving the older baseline variant for a subset of requests and the targeted canary cohort never receives the promoted variant.

Impact: Customer facing — some production users see degraded content quality and behavior changes; increased error rate observed in evaluation tests tied to the rollout. Approx 2–4% of BrightHealth requests in the impacted window were routed to the wrong variant. Potential compliance risk for enterprise tenant due to unexpected model outputs.

Environment: prod-us-west (primary), us-east (secondary failover). Tenant uses reserved capacity with version pin configured via the Console rollout API.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer promotes model gptj-redwood-v2-16k:2026-03-09-12 to canary for 10% cohort.
2) Simulate sustained spike that triggers regional spillover to standby pool (we used internal chaos runner).
3) Observe routing logs and tenant affinity records for handed-off sessions.
4) Notice that pinned_version field is missing from the routing context after the handoff for some cohort tokens.

Observed behavior: After standby handoff, requests for pinned tenant occasionally resolve to baseline variant; canary cohort does not receive promoted variant. Routing logs show standby pool applied fallback-priority mapping which omitted the tenant pin header when shard_id changed.

Expected behavior: Tenant pin should be preserved across standby/standby-promote handoffs so pinned sessions and canary cohort continue to receive the correct promoted variant.

Workaround: Re-apply an explicit version pin for the tenant via Console (immediate but manual). Short term, avoid promoting new canaries during known regional prewarm/spillover windows.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:12 (Maya): Customer first reported inconsistency via Support chat; attached snippet of request IDs and timestamps.
2026-03-10 15:00 (SRE): Correlated request IDs to edge routing traces; observed 'pin' key present entering edge but absent on standby-upstream boundary for ~2-4% of sessions.

2026-03-10 16:20 (Eng - Carlos): Reproduced with chaos runner by forcing shard reshuffle; confirmed that standy-priority mapping table lookup returns fallback set that excludes tenant_pin header when shard_id mismatch occurs.
2026-03-11 09:05 (Eng): Added additional logging in control-plane to capture pin propagation during handoff; logs sent to #support and linked PR for analysis.
2026-03-11 12:30 (Data): Tokenization & eval checks showed content-delta consistent with variant mismatch rather than generation nondeterminism.

Hypothesis: A routing optimization intended to reduce standby config size prunes pinned metadata when it detects nonlocal shard ownership; logic incorrectly treats tenant_pin as ephemeral metadata rather than strong-binding state.

Carlos Ortega (2026-03-10): Running isolated repro with chaos runner; I can recreate at ~3% rate. Opening quick diagnostic PR to add pin-forward flag. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1024
SRE (Anjali Patel) (2026-03-11): Deployed temporary logging to capture metadata stripping; added alert for pin-loss >0.5% for any enterprise tenant in prod-us-west.

Carlos Ortega (2026-03-12): Hotfix candidate merged to canary-edge branch (pr/1031) that marks tenant_pin as required state during standby handoff. Scheduling canary rollout to us-west tonight at low traffic window.
resolution:
Mitigated via hotfix: restored propagation of tenant pin metadata during standby handoffs by updating standby-priority mapping codepath to treat tenant_pin as strong-binding state. Hotfix merged to canary-edge and scheduled for staged rollout in us-west (2026-03-12 23:00 PST). Workaround: re-apply explicit pin via Console for high-risk tenants until rollover completes.

Postmortem/next steps:
- Create unit tests for pin propagation across shard reshuffle (owned by routing team).
- Add an invariant check in control-plane snapshot merge to assert tenant_pin presence for pinned tenants.
- Run customer-targeted canary validation suite for BrightHealth (owned by Solutions Eng).
- Follow-up page with runbook additions: update Standby Routing Runbook to include pin-preservation checklist.

Linked PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1024, https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1031
final_notes: Customer acknowledged interim mitigation and requested a short postmortem after rollout completes. Monitoring set for 72 hours post-deploy; assigned to Carlos for verification and Confluence update.
